asof: Settles Mon 2 Nov 2026 · written Tue 3 Nov
headline: Oil's 7.6% slide bull-steepens SR3 as 2029 contracts drop 3bp; U7 peak 4.51% still prices about two more hikes.
summary: The strip rallied from the back on Monday: U6 and Z6 fell only 0.25bp and 0.5bp in implied rate to 3.92% and 4.14%, H7 to U7 fell 1bp, and the 2029 contracts led with M9, U9 and Z9 each down 3bp to 4.365–4.37%. As the first session of November, those moves are also the week- and month-to-date changes; against the 23 October settle U7 is 10bp and Z7 12bp lower. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.51%, 56bp over the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing, with 14.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is still roughly one hike more than the Fed's median and the consensus call of a December hike followed by a long hold.
drivers: Brent settled $8.66 (7.6%) lower at $104.77 and WTI $7.66 lower at $96.46 after Iran said its leadership had authorised peace talks and Qatari mediation continued. Long Treasury yields fell 4–6bp to the lowest since September, and in SR3 the bid was in 2028–29, where H8 to Z9 fell 1.5–3bp.
Strong ISM keeps the front pinned

ISM manufacturing rose to 55.5 from 54.5, above the roughly 54.6–54.7 expected, with production at its highest since November 2021. Prices paid eased to 75.2 from 77.9 but has been above 70 for nine months, so the front barely moved: Z6 fell 0.5bp and the 2-year yield only about 1bp intraday.

Treasury put October–December borrowing at $618bn, $10bn below its August estimate, on a larger starting cash balance of $984bn, and $800bn for January–March with a $1trn end-March cash target. That keeps bill supply heavy but not worse than feared ahead of Wednesday's refunding, where dealers focus on long-end buybacks.

SOFR printed 3.95% for 30 October, 7bp over the 3.88% EFFR and above the 3.90% interest on reserves, as month-end and coupon settlement pressure carried into November. U6 at 3.92% implied still sits under the fixing.
spreads: The curve bull-steepened beyond the peak while the whites were steady. U6/Z6 slipped 0.25bp to +22bp, Z6/H7 0.5bp to +20.5bp, H7/M7 held at +12.5bp and M7/U7 at +4bp, while U7/Z7 eased 0.5bp to −3bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 narrowed 1bp to +34bp and Z6/M7 0.5bp to +33bp. Past the peak the inversion deepened: Z7/Z8 −1bp to −8.5bp, U7/Z8 −1.5bp to −11.5bp and Z8/Z9 −0.5bp to −3bp, while Z7/H8 held at −3bp. Flies were steady, H7/M7/U7 unchanged at +8.5bp and M7/U7/Z7 up 0.5bp to +7bp. All changes are day, week and month-to-date at once, as Monday is the first November session.
fed: There is no Monday fed funds futures snapshot yet; the latest, dated 30 October and so also the month-end level, prices 17.6bp for the 9 December meeting (a 70% chance of a hike), 24bp by January, 37.3bp by March, 52.1bp by June and a 57bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.45%). That compares with 19.7bp, 42.4bp and a 65bp peak a day earlier, 21.5bp, 43.9bp and 68.5bp on 23 October, and 30.6bp, 63.4bp and 94bp at end-September. SR3 agrees with ZQ at the peak: 4.45% plus SOFR's 7bp premium over EFFR is about 4.52%, level with U7 at 4.51%, though Z6 at 4.14% is about 5bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium, a softer read of December. The strip still prices about two more hikes; the Fed's median projects one more this year and none in 2027, and payrolls on Friday (about 63,000–65,000 expected) are the next test.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 5bp in favour at +33bp after narrowing 0.5bp on Monday, as M7 fell 1bp in rate against 0.5bp for Z6. With 13bp to target and 7bp to the stop, reward is about 1.9 times risk. Kept: cheaper oil and a ZQ peak cut to 57bp from 94bp at end-September support one hike and a hold, not the extra 2027 move M7 still carries.
ideas.risk: A strong payrolls print on Friday or a breakdown in Iran talks that sends oil back toward $118 could push the spread back toward +40bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open at −8.5bp, now 0.5bp in favour after a further 1bp gain on Monday, when Z8's implied rate fell 2.5bp against 1.5bp for Z7. Only 11.5bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9; the target is 16.5bp away against 10.5bp to the stop, about 1.6 times. Keep at about half the core size: it has gained on both the risk-off and the oil-down days.
ideas.risk: If 2027 hikes keep coming out the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through the settlement week

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 settled at 3.92% implied, 0.25bp lower on the day, while the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing sits 3bp above it and above the 3.90% interest on reserves. Thursday's heavy bill settlement could keep fixings firm, and only U6's final week sees the December decision; revisit after the 5 November prints.
ideas.risk: If month-end pressure fades quickly, SOFR could drop back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a couple of bp on the table.

watch: Control of Congress shapes the fiscal and term-premium outlook for the reds, and analysts flag escalation risk with Iran after the vote.
Coupon sizes, buybacks and the bill share drive the reds and funding; services prices test the 2027 hikes.
Bill settlement; jobless claims; Fed's Barkin and Logan
A heavy settlement day for SOFR and U6; Logan has called for at least two more hikes.
October payrolls; Fed's Williams and Bowman
About 63,000–65,000 expected after 29,000; the main test for Z6/M7, with Williams the key voice.
ZQ prices 17.6bp, a 70% chance of a hike; the outcome sets Z6 and the whites.
Brent at $104.77 after a 7.6% fall; a deal or a post-election strike would swing the 2027 hikes priced.
